title: Zero-harmonic homological inversion is possible only with an optimal two-derivative cost

derivative_boundary.homological_multiplier: For fixed p!=0 define T_p by (T_p f)(k)=Phi_q(k,p)^(-1) f(k)
derivative_boundary.upper_bound: The exact K1442 identity gives Phi_q(k,p)^(-1)<=C_(p,M_q)<k>^2, so T_p maps h^(s+2) continuously to h^s
derivative_boundary.optimality: Along lattice-parallel k=j p, Phi_q(k,p)^(-1) is asymptotic to 2|k|^2/(M_q^2 |p|); no h^(s+alpha) to h^s bound with alpha<2 is possible
derivative_boundary.finite_tier_cauchy_consequence: If cutoff forcing f_N is Cauchy in h^(s+2), then T_p f_N is Cauchy in h^s for each fixed nonzero Maxwell mode p
derivative_boundary.same_tier_boundary: Strict zero-harmonic nonresonance removes K1435's exact resonance but does not restore a same-tier bounded normal form
derivative_boundary.full_pde_ceiling: The scalar fixed-p multiplier does not include the differentiated current numerator, the sum over Maxwell modes, nonlinear composition, gauge constraints, semibounded energy, or a cutoff-uniform global flow
